notes: A band is a measure's acceptable range. tool: the bench that checks it; theatre, faction and posture narrow an air_war_balance band (empty: any). Shares are 0-1, latencies minutes, exchanges our fighters lost for each of theirs (the US view) in air_war_bench and theirs lost for each of ours in air_war_balance. A band from a historical count is about its 95 per cent interval, widened where the analogue is flown with other types; a game value says so.

fain_1988_posture pp. D-13, D-14 (the defender changed posture, forced back, in 29 of 59 WWII divisional engagements of about 3 days) and fig. VI-6 (a division's defence gives way at about 40 per cent losses); mt_stashek_losses p. 7, mt_novoselov_replacement p. 9 (ours withdraw only when ineffective, on the senior's order). The upper bound the engagements' half, the lower a game value: a war of two weeks withdraws at least one division of twenty engaged. F6.1: our formations a day or more in the fight, of them withdrawn as a unit or dispersed. Argued (F6.1): none withdrawn; our formations are in the fight 3-5 days, end at 84-88 per cent of their establishment (repairs returned, reinforced), never at the sourced line of half (mt_stashek_losses) nor fain_1988_posture's defender breakpoint of about 40 per cent losses. Re-argued (F7.3, measured): at their lowest hour in the war our formations a day in the fight stand at 84 per cent of establishment on average (the lowest 73, none under the degraded line of two thirds) against the ask line of half: they lose 6.9 per cent a day in contact, in their band, but for about 3 days each (17 formation-days in contact a war for 6 formations), 32 per cent by every cause, 21 points given back by repairs and columns. With the repair return at 0 (a sensitivity run) the lowest is still 72 per cent on average (62 the lowest) and none withdraws: the return is not what keeps them up, the days in contact are. The rule is applied as sourced (a formation's own count under half, mt_stashek_losses); the band's upper anchor, the engagements in which the defender was forced back (fain_1988_posture), is a posture change by the fight's outcome, which this model gives as the line pushed in (every Pact axis reaches its objective) with the formation intact, not as a withdrawal by the loss line

fain_1988_posture pp. D-13, D-14, fig. VI-6; mt_stashek_losses p. 7 (as against the Pact). Argued (F6.1): none withdrawn; our formations end at 82-84 per cent of their establishment, never at the sourced line of half (mt_stashek_losses) nor fain_1988_posture's defender breakpoint of about 40 per cent losses. Re-argued (F7.3, measured): at their lowest hour our formations a day in the fight stand at 75 per cent on average (the lowest 64; 3 of 9 under the degraded line of two thirds, none under the ask line of half); 5.0 per cent a day in contact for about 7 days each, 38 per cent by every cause, 22 points given back by repairs and columns. With the repair return at 0 the lowest is 66 per cent on average (55 the lowest) and still none withdraws: two weeks of NATO's slow attack at its loss rate do not bring a formation to half, whatever the return

reznichenko_1984 pp. 177-179 and vr_poltikovic_1984 p. 96 (a penetration is met by the senior's counterattack with the second echelon or reserve); fain_1988_posture pp. D-13, D-14 (the defender forced the attacker's posture change in 30 of 59 engagements). The lower bound a game value. F6.1: of the wars in which the enemy reached our main defensive zone (F7.1: or halted on our ground), those in which our army counterattacked. Argued (F7.1): none; the army's reserve (its tank brigade, 12.5 per cent of the army, held 55 km back, fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 2-11) and every other free formation come to 0.28 of the enemy at a Pact penetration's tip at best (0.29 in the 245 h a war its momentum is spent), against the army commander's 1.8-2.2: a front of three divisions on one axis outweighs our whole free force even at its one breakthrough sector. Re-argued (F7.3): the same, 0.28 (0.29 in 245 h a war) on F7.1-F7.2: the air front's step behind the Pact's axes (F7.2) does not wear its tip down (the enemy's division loses 1.57 per cent a day in contact, as before). Even the ratio's sourced floor, 1.5, would need 5.4 times our free force; the counterattack reznichenko_1984 describes is the senior's second echelon or reserve sized for it, a front's, and our order of battle has one army against a front: a front reserve is a force-structure decision, not a value to tune. Green (F8.1): the national command's reserve, the 11th Tank Division (data/campaign/ground_defence.json front_reserve), committed by the front's commander with every free force in his 24 h reach: a counterstrike in 3 of 3 wars, ordered on 2.03 at the tip by his picture. It wins back no ground: the Pact's axes are halted in towns in hasty defence, 0.75-0.90 in the combat (docs/fronts/06_BALANCE.md, As built: F8.1); the band counts the counterattack, not its success

reznichenko_1984 pp. 177-179; vr_poltikovic_1984 p. 96; fain_1988_posture pp. D-13, D-14 (as against the Pact). Argued (F7.1): none; the army's reserve and every other free formation come to 0.51 of the enemy at a NATO penetration's tip at best (0.52 in the 300 h a war its momentum is spent), against the army commander's 1.8-2.2: NATO's corps puts a whole division's first echelon at the tip. Re-argued (F7.3): the same, 0.51 (0.52 in 300 h a war) on F7.1-F7.2, NATO's war unchanged by F7.2 (its air front never steps); the ratio's sourced floor, 1.5, would need 2.9 times our free force: a front or national reserve is a force-structure decision, not a value to tune. Green (F8.1): the 11th Tank Division committed by the front's commander: a counterstrike in 3 of 3 wars, ordered on 2.05 at the tip by his picture; it wins back no ground (NATO's axis halted in a town, the strikes at night, 0.82 in the combat; docs/fronts/06_BALANCE.md, As built: F8.1)
